subject.title: Bug: Poe image/video-output models are accepted in config but fail at runtime (Nano Banana 400, Veo/Sora fallback)

question: Should configured Poe image/video-output models be explicitly rejected as unsupported session chat models for now, or should OpenClaw add first-class media-output model routing?
rationale: The short-term rejection path and the full media-output runtime path are both plausible, but they create different public config, provider capability, fallback, and channel-rendering contracts.

options.title: Reject media-output chat models for now
options.body: Add validation and runtime diagnostics that make text-output session support explicit while leaving image/video generation on provider-tool paths until a fuller design exists.

options.title: Add media-output runtime support
options.body: Extend schema, model selection, response handling, and channel rendering so configured image/video-output models can produce media directly in sessions.

options.title: Track in broader provider capability design
options.body: Keep this as product-design input while a larger model modality and provider capability contract is planned.

recommendation.title: Reject media-output chat models for now
recommendation.body: Add validation and runtime diagnostics that make text-output session support explicit while leaving image/video generation on provider-tool paths until a fuller design exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history ties this boundary to the image_generate/media-tool and current model/config surfaces that must change for either direction.
